executive_summary: This chapter introduces the concept of geometric congruence in plane figures, focusing specifically on triangles. Figures are defined as congruent if they have identical shape and size, meaning one can be superimposed onto another through translation, rotation, or reflection to fit exactly. The chapter systematically builds criteria for triangle congruence: SSS (Side-Side-Side), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), ASA (Angle-Side-Angle) / AAS (Angle-Angle-Side), and RHS (Right-Hypotenuse-Side) for right-angled triangles. It emphasizes vertex correspondence (order of vertices in congruence notation like ΔABC ≅ ΔXYZ) and explores properties such as equal angles opposite to equal sides in isosceles triangles and 60° angles in equilateral triangles.
key_takeaways: Congruence (≅): Relation between two figures having the exact same shape and exact same size.
SSS Criterion: If three sides of one triangle equal three sides of another, Δ1 ≅ Δ2.
SAS Criterion: If two sides and the included angle equal two sides and the included angle, Δ1 ≅ Δ2.
ASA / AAS Criterion: If two angles and one side equal two angles and the corresponding side, Δ1 ≅ Δ2.
